name: North Dakota
$scopeNote: WIRED TO CALC CODE (a later 'go to every state, look for what's missing' pass): originally a DATA-ONLY pass (Scott: 'do the Dakotas and the Virginias, just for the data'); northDakotaWithholding() in src/taxes/state.ts now dispatches both vintages for real. North Dakota has one of the lowest real income tax rates in the country (0% / 1.95% / 2.50%, three brackets, genuinely close to Idaho/Iowa in simplicity) but a genuinely two-track withholding SYSTEM depending on which vintage of Form W-4 the employee has on file -- a structural complexity Iowa is the only other state in this project to have (its formVintage dispatch). Wiring this in surfaced a real transcription bug, fixed in the same pass: see annualBrackets.bracketNote below.

sources.title: North Dakota Office of State Tax Commissioner -- Income Tax Withholding Rates and Instructions, 2025 Calendar Year
sources.quote: Married Filing Jointly ... $ 0 $ 55,488 ... 164,038 ... 2,116.73 + 2.50% ... Head of Household ... 76,200 282,700 ... 4,026.75 + 2.50% ... Single ... 55,975 252,325 ... 3,828.83 + 2.50% ... One withholding allowance--Weekly ... $97.00 ... Multiply the supplemental wages by 1.50%

sources.title: U.S. Department of Labor, ETA -- Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective January 2025

withholdingStructure.$comment: Two fully separate methods depending on which W-4 vintage is on file -- North Dakota's own booklet titles them Section 1 and Section 2. A newly hired employee with NO Form W-4 on file uses Section 2, treated as Single -- this is the modern default, not Section 1.

section1_preFederal2020W4.appliesWhen: Employee's Form W-4 on file predates the 2020 federal redesign (still uses withholding allowances).
section1_preFederal2020W4.mechanism: Subtract (number of allowances x a flat per-period allowance dollar amount) from gross wages, then look up the result in a filing-status-specific (Single-including-HoH, or Married) bracket table for the pay period. Rounds to the NEAREST WHOLE DOLLAR -- the same whole-dollar convention this project's Maine file uses, genuinely unusual among states built so far (most round to the cent).

annualBrackets.bracketNote: Transcribed verbatim from Table 7 (Annual Payroll Period). Single's own table oddly prints '$0' for both the first AND second row's base before the excess-rate column, but the worked mechanics (confirmed against Table 1-6's algebra: e.g. weekly base $75.31 at $1,108 = 1.95% x $3,862-ish scaled -- internally consistent) make clear the true structure is 0% up to $57,625, then 1.95% on the excess up to $258,450, then a fixed $3,916.09 base plus 2.50% above that -- i.e. only TWO effective rates (0%, 1.95%, 2.50%), not three independently-based tiers. Recorded as 3 rows for shape-consistency with this project's other bracket tables (WIBracket-style), with the middle row's base correctly $0 since it starts exactly where the 0% bracket ends. BUG FIXED (wiring pass): the Single table's first bracket had rate 0.0195 here, not 0 -- inconsistent with this very prose AND with Section 2's own Single table below, which covers the identical boundaries and correctly has rate 0 on the first bracket. Corrected to 0.

section1_preFederal2020W4.note: Full per-period tables (weekly/biweekly/semimonthly/monthly/quarterly/semiannual/daily) are published directly by ND -- NOT derived from the annual figures by simple division the way Iowa's were provably shown to be; not independently re-verified this pass that ND's own per-period tables are exact prorations of the annual ones (a real open question, not assumed either way).

section2_2020AndLaterW4.appliesWhen: Employee's Form W-4 is 2020-or-later vintage, OR a newly hired employee has submitted no Form W-4 at all (treated as Single by ND's own instruction, matching this project's standing no-certificate-default convention for once being a state-stated rule rather than an inferred one).
section2_2020AndLaterW4.mechanism: Genuinely distinct from every other state in this project: there is NO ND-specific exemption/allowance subtraction step at all. The employer takes the employee's TAXABLE WAGES FOR THE PAY PERIOD (i.e. wages already net of whatever the federal Form W-4's own Steps 2-4c produced -- multiple-jobs adjustment, dependents credit converted to a wage-equivalent reduction, other income, deductions), annualizes by the pay-period count, and looks the ANNUAL figure up directly in one of THREE filing-status tables (Married Filing Jointly / Head of Household / Single) pulled straight from the employee's Form W-4 Step 1(c) checkbox. Because the input is already the FEDERALLY-adjusted wage figure, 401(k)/125/HSA-type pretax deferrals are excluded from the ND base BY CONSTRUCTION, not by any separate ND statute or rule -- the strongest possible confidence tier for exemptPretax conformity, stronger than every other state's federal-AGI-conformity finding in this project, since there's no intermediate 'ND adjusted gross income' concept to independently verify -- the federal number IS the ND number at this step.
section2_2020AndLaterW4.worksheetSteps: Booklet's own Percentage Method Worksheet: (1) taxable wages this period, (2) periods/year, (3) annualize (1x2), (4) look up annual withholding from the filing-status table, (5) divide line 4 by line 2 for the per-period amount, rounded to the nearest whole dollar -- same whole-dollar rounding convention as Section 1.

withholdingStructure.supplementalWages: Booklet has a dedicated Section 3 (page 57) for supplemental wages, not read in detail this pass -- flagged as an open item below rather than guessed at.

roundingComment: Both Section 1 and Section 2 round to the nearest whole dollar per the booklet's own text (see worksheetSteps above) -- handled generically via rules.roundFinalToWholeDollar in stateIncomeTax(), the same mechanism built for Maine and reused by several other states in this project.

reciprocity.mechanism: Form NDW-R, filed by the employee with the employer (due by Feb 28 or within 30 days of hire/address change; employer mails to the state by Mar 31; must be refiled annually).
reciprocity.rule: A Minnesota or Montana resident working in North Dakota is exempt from ND withholding on those wages, provided NDW-R is on file.
reciprocity.confidence: The existence and MN/MT scope of the agreement is confirmed by the form's own title, fetched directly. The specific mechanics (deadlines, annual refiling) are cross-source only this pass -- NDW-R's own instructions text was not read line-by-line, unlike this project's usual standard for a reciprocity mechanism (e.g. Kansas's KW-100 worked example, Ohio's IT 4NR).

localIncomeTax.rule: NONE. Cross-source confirmed: no North Dakota city, county, or municipality levies a tax on wages or earned income.
localIncomeTax.confidence: cross_source_confirmed, not tied to a specific enabling/prohibiting statute citation this pass.

paidLeave.rule: NONE, and structurally locked out at the local level too: North Dakota has no mandatory state Paid Family/Medical Leave program, and (a genuinely distinctive fact among every state in this project so far) North Dakota law affirmatively PREEMPTS cities and counties from enacting their OWN mandatory paid-leave ordinances -- not merely an absence of a state program the way most no-PFML states in this project are, but a state-level ceiling that forecloses the Wilmington/JEDD-style local patchwork risk this project has flagged in other states.
paidLeave.confidence: cross_source_confirmed via search synthesis, not independently read from the ND Century Code preemption provision itself this pass.

exemptPretaxComment: FIXED (wiring pass): this field was previously stored as a note object, not an array, which would have thrown ('object is not iterable') the moment any calc code called ctx.taxableWagesFor() against this ruleset -- caught by the first test run, not by inspection. Set to the standard exclusion list this project uses everywhere else. For Section 2 (2020+ W-4) this is doubly justified: the ND base IS whatever wage figure the federal W-4 process already produced, so pretax deferrals are excluded by construction regardless of this list. Section 1 (pre-2020 W-4) relies on this list directly, consistent with every other state's federal-conformity-based exemptPretax -- not independently re-derived from a North Dakota-specific statute this pass.

certificateFields.section2_2020Plus: Default path (formVintage unset or anything else). No separate ND certificate -- status is read directly from input.federalW4.filingStatus per the booklet's own instruction that it comes 'straight from the employee's Form W-4 Step 1(c) checkbox.' federalW4.filingStatus 'married_separate' resolves to the Single table (the 2020+ federal form bundles Single/MFS into one checkbox), same convention as New Mexico.

knownGaps: Descriptive notes carried from the 2026 file (reciprocity, local-tax rules, method comments) were checked against the 2025 source for the fields this engine computes from; narrative text that only describes 2026 history should be read as background.

suiEmployer.$comment: Normalized employer-side unemployment parameters — the shape src/taxes/state.ts reads. The detailed unemploymentInsurance block above stays the record of research; this exists because that block's shape varies too much between states to compute from directly (wage bases as objects, industry-keyed rate maps, differently-named keys).
suiEmployer.wageBaseSource: DOL Significant Provisions, January 2025 (Wages Subject to Tax)
suiEmployer.newEmployerRateSource: DOL Significant Provisions, January 2025 (New Employer Rate, base rate)

supplementalWages.$comment: ND Section 3, Option 1: "Multiply the supplemental wages by 1.50% (.0150)." An employer option (Option 2, aggregation, is the alternative) -- matching Missouri's own dual-method shape in this project.

supplementalAggregation.source: ND Section 3, Option 2: aggregate with the most recent regular payroll period, tax the combined amount, subtract tax already withheld on the regular portion.

$yearNote: 2025 ruleset: 1.95% and 2.5% above $55,975 (single) / $55,488 (married) / $76,200 (head of household) a year; the pre-2020 W-4 allowance is $97 a week ($5,050 a year), and supplemental wages may be withheld at a flat 1.5%.
